name: Villages with Fortified Churches in Transylvania
description: In southern Transylvania, Romania, seven villages are listed for their fortified churches, built between the 13th and 16th centuries. Six were founded by Transylvanian Saxon settlers and one by the Székely. Each church rises above its village behind thick defensive walls, and the farmsteads below still follow the layout of the late Middle Ages. These seven were picked from more than 150 surviving examples.
